Question:
Each of the points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) \(E,\) and \(F\) in the figure below represents a different digit from \(1\) to \(6.\) Each of the five lines shown passes through some of these points. The digits along each line are added to produce five sums, one for each line. The total of the five sums is \(47.\) What is the digit represented by \(B?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2020_AMC_8_Q16_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
Instead of finding all six digits, count how often each digit appears when the five line sums are added.

The figure shows these five sums:

\[
\begin{aligned}
&A+B+C,\quad A+F+E,\\
&B+D,\quad B+F,\quad C+D+E.
\end{aligned}
\]

Every point appears twice except \(B\), which appears three times. The total is therefore

\[
2(A+B+C+D+E+F)+B=47.
\]

The six digits are \(1\) through \(6\), so their sum is \(21\). Thus \(42+B=47\), giving \(\boxed{B=5}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\). Counting appearances reveals the extra copy of \(B\) without assigning the other digits.
